# Cover art

> Overview type `cover_art` (since 1.0). Entity: required, a `media_player` entity. Card type `custom:houseview-cover-art-overview-card` (widget type `cover_art_overview`), screensaver `type: cover_art`.

The album cover of the track that is playing, full screen on black: a big rounded square inset a few percent from the
edges, the track title bottom left over the picture and the artist beneath it. The black frame around the square is
part of the look. It also works as a page card or a standalone card (`custom:houseview-cover-art-overview-card`; a tap
on the card opens the speaker's more-info dialog).

It is an **automatic display**: nothing needs choosing in the configuration. For every `media_player` widget on the
carousel an implicit idle entry is added, so a speaker that has been playing while nobody touches the screen shows its
cover instead of the usual screensaver.

```yaml
# This is all it takes: a music widget and the weather as the everyday screensaver.
type: custom:houseview-card
cards:
  - type: custom:houseview-media_player-card
    entity: media_player.living_room
screensaver:
  type: weather
  entity: weather.home
```

Weather (or any other idle screensaver you wrote) stays the default. Cover art only wins at the moment the idle time is
up **and** a speaker is playing with a usable cover (priority 10 against weather's 0, plus the overview's `eligible`
rule). Otherwise the screensaver you configured starts as before, and with no `screensaver` block at all and nothing
playing, nothing starts. The idle time is the `idle_timeout` of your first explicit idle entry, else 120 seconds: an
implicit entry never sets one of its own. While the music widget is on the page that is showing and its speaker is
playing, the idle time is shortened to 5 seconds, so the cover appears soon after you stop touching the music page.

Turn it off with `music_screensaver: false` on the card, or give a list of `media_player` entities to replace the ones
taken from the widgets (see [overviews and screensavers](../screensavers.md)). To use it explicitly, for another entity:

```yaml
screensaver:
  - type: weather
    entity: weather.home
  - type: cover_art
    entity: media_player.kitchen
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entity | entity | required | A `media_player.*` entity |
| name | text | | Used for a player that names no track |

There are no look options on purpose: the face is one picture. The framework keys apply (`enabled`, `preview`,
`start_in_edit_mode`, and `idle_timeout` on an explicit entry).

## What is shown

| Speaker state | Face | Eligible as a screensaver | While it is on screen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `playing`, with a cover | the cover, title, artist | yes | stays |
| `playing`, no usable cover | a dark square with a large music note, title, artist | no | stays |
| `paused` | the same face | no | stays |
| `buffering` | the same face (the gap between two tracks) | no | stays |
| `idle`, `off`, `standby` | black, "Nothing playing" | no | goes away at once |
| unavailable, unknown, missing | black, "Nothing playing" | no | goes away at once |

* **Eligible** means `state: playing` **and** the entity names a usable cover. When it is not eligible at the moment
  the idle time is up, the next entry (weather) is shown; with nothing eligible nothing is shown and the idle time
  starts over.
* **Goes away** is the overview's `autoWake`: no tap swallow, the dashboard is back at once. A paused speaker keeps the
  face, so pausing for a minute does not bring the dashboard back.
* **Track changes** are patched in place: the title, the artist and the picture change on the next render, and the
  browser keeps painting the old cover until the new one has loaded. No flash.
* A tap on the screensaver only closes it. Nothing here calls a service.

## The cover

The picture is `attributes.entity_picture`, and only when it comes from the page's own origin (or Home Assistant's
configured base URL) **and** a path under `/api/media_player_proxy/`. Anything else, a foreign address, `data:` or
`javascript:` URLs, is ignored and never loaded. Home Assistant puts the remote address in `entity_picture` for players
whose pictures are reachable from outside and keeps the proxy address in `entity_picture_local`: that one is used when
`entity_picture` is not usable.

Text is `media_title` (then `media_channel`; a player that reports nothing shows its own name) and `media_artist` (then
`media_album_artist`, then `media_series_title`). It is always text, never markup.

## The look

The square is 88.4% of the smaller side of the screen, centred (a 5.8% black margin all round), with corners of 12.5% of
its side. The title is 5.8% of the square (semibold white, up to two lines), the artist 3.8% (62% white, one line,
ellipsis). The same markup fits a landscape tablet (black bars either side), a portrait tablet, a phone and a small card.

## Cost

Painted with CSS only: one `<img>` with `object-fit: cover`, one static `linear-gradient` scrim and two lines of text.
No blur, no `filter`, no `backdrop-filter`, no shadow, no animation and no JavaScript beyond the patch on a state
change, so it makes no difference between `performance` modes and has no motion to reduce.
